'''Project-76''', also referred to as '''P76''', is an initiative by India's [[Ministry of Defence (India)|Ministry of Defence]] (MoD) to develop diesel-electric [[submarine]]s for the [[Indian Navy]] (IN). The submarine is being developed by the [[Defence Research and Development Organisation]] (DRDO).<ref name="TP76">{{Cite news |author=Snehesh Alex Phillip |date=2022-07-18 |title=India's submarine plans hit by dwindling fleet as Navy decommissions INS Sindhudhvaj |url=https://theprint.in/defence/indias-submarine-plans-hit-by-dwindling-fleet-as-navy-decommissions-ins-sindhudhvaj/1043167/ |access-date=2022-09-03 |newspaper=The Print |location=New Delhi}}</ref>

== Background ==
{{Main|Submarine-building Perspective Plan}}
In 1997, the [[Cabinet Committee on Security]] (CCS) — the final decision-making body of the [[Government of India]] on all matters of India's [[national security]] chaired by the [[Prime Minister of India|Prime Minister]] — approved the construction of two [[Type 209 submarine|Type 209/1500]] attack submarines (SSK) at a then-estimated cost of [[Indian rupee|INR]] ₹700 crore. This effort, which was conceived in the wake of an [[Shishumar-class submarine#Corruption charges|international corruption scandal]] related to India's acquisition of the [[Shishumar-class submarine|''Shishumar''-class submarines]], called for the construction of two Type 209/1500 SSKs at [[Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders|Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited]] (MDL) with the assistance of a foreign naval firm in a corroborative role. In accordance with the scheme, the [[Indian Navy]] (IN) and MDL approached several naval enterprises for assistance; however, the French-based [[Thomson-CSF]] (TCSF) was the only firm willing to participate.<ref name="SSK History2">{{Cite web |title=Undue favour to vendor in acquisition of submarines - Ministry Of Defence - Public Accounts Committee (2009-10) |url=https://eparlib.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/64525/1/15_Public_Accounts_10.pdf |url-status= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231225085545/https://eparlib.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/64525/1/15_Public_Accounts_10.pdf |archive-date=2023-12-25 |website=eparlib.nic.in}}</ref>

Two years later, on 12 July 1999, the Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS) approved a two-phase plan to build 24 submarines over a span of 30 years.<ref>{{Cite press release |title=Submarine Construction Project |date=2014-12-12 |publisher=[[Press Information Bureau]] |url=https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=113213&reg=3&lang=1 |access-date=2026-01-10 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260110165601/https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=113213&reg=3&lang=2 |archive-date=2026-01-10}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-05-18 |title=Navy seeks amendment to 30-year submarine plan, wants six nuclear boats |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/navy-seeks-amendment-to-30-year-submarine-plan-wants-six-nuclear-boats-101621307478586.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260110055552/https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/navy-seeks-amendment-to-30-year-submarine-plan-wants-six-nuclear-boats-101621307478586.html |archive-date=2026-01-10 |access-date=2026-01-10 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}}</ref> The plan was named 'Project for Series Construction of Submarines for the Indian Navy and Acquisition of National Competence in Submarine Building', also referred as '[[Submarine-building Perspective Plan]]'. For the first phase, six submarines each were to be built at MDL under [[Project 75]] (P-75) along with a parallel [[production line]] of another public/private shipyard<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 2018 |title=24 Submarines in 30 Years? |url=https://www.spsnavalforces.com/story/?id=257 |website=www.spsnavalforces.com}}</ref> under [[Project-75 (India) submarine acquisition project|Project-75 (India)]] or P-75(I) with [[technology transfer]]. Under the second phase, twelve submarines would be built including complete indigenous design, development and construction of submarines in India.<ref name="SSK History2" /><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Vavasseur |first=Xavier |date=2021-11-10 |title=MDL Delivers 4th Scorpene Submarine to the Indian Navy |url=https://www.navalnews.com/naval-news/2021/11/mdl-delivers-4th-scorpene-submarine-to-the-indian-navy/ |access-date=2026-01-10 |website=Naval News |language=en-US}}</ref> While the first phase was scheduled for completion within 2012, the second phase would be executed in 2012–2030.<ref name=":6" />

For the '''[[Project 75|Project-75]]''', two options emerged. The first being construction of the Type 209/1500 at MDL initially with the combat suite of TCSF with the rest being based on [[Scorpène-class submarine|modified ''Scorpène'' submarine design]] based on Naval requirements. The second option recommended the construction of all the SSKs based on the newer ''Scorpène'' design. Ultimately, the Naval Heqadquarters chose the latter, reasoning that the ''Scorpène'', which had been offered with a provision of [[technology transfer]] (TOT), was more advanced than the Type 209/1500. The initial plan to ally with TCSF was dropped in April 2001 and negotiations for the procurement of the ''Scorpène'' design under the first phase, dubbed Project-75 (P-75), began in November 2001. The ''Scorpène'' design was offered by another French-based naval firm, Armaris (later [[Naval Group|DCNS]], now [[Naval Group]]).<ref name="SSK History2" /> The P-75 contract signed on 6 October 2005<ref name="thbl-20feb062">{{cite news |date=20 February 2006 |title=Envisaging more defence ties |url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/todays-paper/tp-others/tp-states/Envisaging-more-defence-ties/article20199367.ece |url-status= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180430015835/https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/todays-paper/tp-others/tp-states/Envisaging-more-defence-ties/article20199367.ece |archive-date=30 April 2018 |work=The Hindu Business Line |language=en}}</ref> resulted in the construction of six {{Sclass|Kalvari|submarine|1|5=2015}}s<ref name=":0" /> beginning 23 May 2009.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2017-01-10 |title=First of six Scorpene subs country bought in 2005 to be commissioned |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/first-of-six-scorpene-subs-country-bought-in-2005-to-be-commissioned/articleshow/56432661.cms |access-date=2026-01-10 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref> The final unit, {{INS|Vagsheer|S26}}, was commissioned in January 2025.<ref name=":7">{{Cite news |date=2025-01-15 |title=PM Modi commissions INS Surat, INS Nilgiri, and INS Vaghsheer: Key points |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/pm-modi-departs-for-mumbai-to-dedicate-naval-combatants-inaugurate-iskcon-temple/articleshow/117251565.cms |access-date=2025-01-15 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref>

Though the second batch of six submarines, under [[Project-75 (India) submarine acquisition project|'''Project-75 (India)''']], was to be executed simultaneously alongside P-75, financial constraints within the MoD led to P-75 being the only project sanctioned for six submarines.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 2022 |title=Scorpene Submarines — An Edge for Indian Navy's Submarine Fleet Build-up |url=https://www.spsnavalforces.com/story/?id=804&h=Scorpene-Submarines-An-Edge-for-Indian-Navys-Submarine-Fleet-Build-up |website=www.spsnavalforces.com}}</ref> Proposals to move ahead with the acquisition failed twice after the [[Project-75 (India) submarine acquisition project#Design selection|project was approved in 2010 and 2014]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Pandit |first=Rajat |date=2010-07-11 |title=Biggest military deal: Six subs for Rs 50,000 crore |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/Biggest-military-deal-Six-subs-zfor-Rs-50000-crore/articleshow/6152862.cms |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260110082616/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/Biggest-military-deal-Six-subs-zfor-Rs-50000-crore/articleshow/6152862.cms |archive-date=2026-01-10 |access-date=2026-01-10 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref><ref name=":9">{{Cite web |date=2014-10-26 |title=6 Made-in-India Submarines for Navy for 53,000 Crores |url=https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/6-made-in-india-submarines-for-navy-for-53-000-crores-684137 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260110083151/https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/6-made-in-india-submarines-for-navy-for-53-000-crores-684137 |archive-date=2026-01-10 |access-date=2024-09-14 |website=NDTV.com}}</ref> Following delays, the Navy mandated the presence of an operational [[air-independent propulsion]] (AIP) plant with the submarine design. With the approval of the Project 77, the number of boats under '''[[Project 76 submarine|Project-76]]''' was reduced to six units. The design was expected to inherit elements from the Project-75 and Project-75(I) designs.<ref name=":6" /> The development was cleared by defence ministry in June 2024 followed by a feasibility study conducted by [[DRDO]].<ref name=":11" /> An approval from the [[Cabinet Committee on Security]] (CCS) for the further detailed design of the submarine is due as of February 2025.<ref name=":12" />

Both Project 76 and Project 77 are being led by the [[Advanced Technology Vessel]] headquarters which is responsible for the development and construction of India's [[Nuclear submarine|nuclear-powered]], [[ballistic missile submarine]] fleet including {{Sclass|Arihant|submarine|4}} and {{Sclass|S5|submarine}}s.<ref name=":11" /><ref name=":33" /> While the final two submarines from the ''Arihant'' class is expected to be commissioned in early 2026 and 2027, respectively, the construction of first two units of S5 submarines has also begun in the Shipbuilding Centre (SBC), [[Visakhapatnam]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sharma |first=Shivani |last2=Negi |first2=Manjeet |date=2025-12-02 |title=Navy to get INS Aridhaman, third Indian-made nuclear submarine |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/ins-aridaman-third-indian-made-nuclear-submarine-to-be-commissioned-soon-navy-chief-2829303-2025-12-02 |access-date=2025-12-02 |website=India Today |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":17">{{Cite web |date=2025-12-29 |title=CHAKRA EXCLUSIVE: India's fourth SSBN sails out for sea trials |url=https://chakranewz.com/critical-technologies/trending/chakra-exclusive-india-rsquo-s-fourth-ssbn-sails-out-for-sea-trials |access-date=2025-12-30 |website=Chakranewz |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":20">{{Cite web |date=2026-01-05 |title=Arihant class nuclear-powered submarine S4* likely to be named INS Arisudan |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/arihant-class-nuclear-powered-submarine-s4-likely-to-be-named-ins-arisudan-101767555406284.html |access-date=2026-01-05 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}}</ref>

== Development ==
Naval Design Bureau, under the command of Director General (Naval Design) was working on diesel-electric submarines equipped with [[air-independent propulsion]] (AIP) in 2022.<ref name="TP76" /><ref name=":6">{{Cite web |last=Linganna |first=Girish |date=2022-08-18 |title=Will India's New Submarine Fleet Be Ready by 2030? |url=https://nationalinterest.org/blog/buzz/will-india%E2%80%99s-new-submarine-fleet-be-ready-2030-204272 |access-date=2024-02-24 |website=The National Interest |language=en}}</ref>

On 25 August 2023, [[Mazagon Dock Limited]] (MDL) signed a [[memorandum of understanding]] with Directorate of Naval Design (Submarine Design Group) for collaboration in R&D of technology and equipment for submarine applications.<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1698558429097562399 |user=MazagonDockLtd |title=#MoU between #MDL & DND-SDG for Collaboration in R&D of Technology & Equipment for Submarine Applications. |date=2023-09-04 |access-date=2026-01-10}}</ref><ref name=":10">{{Cite web |last=Menon |first=Adithya Krishna |date=2025-09-15 |title=Indian Navy’s indigenous submarine programs gather steam |url=https://www.navalnews.com/naval-news/2025/09/indian-navys-indigenous-submarine-programs-gather-steam/ |access-date=2026-01-10 |website=Naval News |language=en-US}}</ref>

In July 2024, the [[Defence Research and Development Organisation]] (DRDO) started a one-year feasibility study on the design and development of an indigenous conventional submarine under Project-76. The defence ministry had cleared the project to calculate the "contours". This programme has been taken up on the lines of the [[Advanced Technology Vessel|Advanced Technology Vessel (ATV) project]]. Following the study a formal case will be forwarded to the [[Cabinet Committee on Security]] (CCS) for project sanction. The design would include a high indigenous content including missiles, armament, [[sonar]], communication [[Electronic warfare|equipment]] suite, mast and [[periscope]]. The design will also include the [[Naval Materials Research Laboratory#Phosphoric Acid Fuel Cell-based AIP system|DRDO-developed AIP module]] for the {{Sclass|Kalvari|submarine|1|5=2015}}s. However, the AIP module's current power output of {{Convert|13.5|kW|abbr=on}} would be scaled up to {{Convert|20|kW|abbr=on}} in order to meet the power outputs of future P76 design. The overall AIP is a stack of 24 [[phosphoric acid]] [[Air-independent propulsion#Fuel cells|fuel cells]] (PAFC).<ref name=":11">{{Cite news |last=Peri |first=Dinakar |date=2024-06-30 |title=DRDO takes up preliminary study on development of indigenous conventional submarine |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/drdo-takes-up-preliminary-study-on-development-of-indigenous-conventional-submarine/article68352888.ece |access-date=2025-02-22 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref> The module also includes an on-board Hydrogen generation system.<ref name=":32">{{Cite web |title=DRDO and L&T join hands for Realisation of Indigenous Air Independent Propulsion (AIP) System for Submarines of Indian Navy |url=https://www.larsentoubro.com/pressreleases/2023/2023-06-22-drdo-and-lt-join-hands-for-realisation-of-indigenous-air-independent-propulsion-aip-system-for-submarines-of-indian-navy/ |access-date=2024-12-29 |website=www.larsentoubro.com |language=en}}</ref>

The activation of the programme was part of the 100-day Action Plan of the Ministry of Defence (MoD)<ref>{{Cite press release |title=Shri Rajnath Singh assumes charge as Raksha Mantri for the second consecutive term |date=2024-06-13 |publisher=[[Press Information Bureau]] |url=https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2025004&reg=3&lang=1 |quote=Immediately after assumption of charge, Shri Rajnath Singh chaired a review meeting on the first 100 days’ Action Plan of MoD under the new government led by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. |access-date=2026-01-10}}</ref> following the [[2024 Indian general election|formation of new government]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2024-08-11 |title=MDL surges ahead in India's Rs 60,000 crore submarine project after clearing key trials |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/defence/mdl-surges-ahead-in-indias-rs-60000-crore-submarine-project-after-clearing-key-trials/articleshow/112448280.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2026-01-10 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Philip |first=Snehesh Alex |date=2024-04-04 |title=Indian Navy team in Germany to inspect AIP tech for new submarines, Spain next |url=https://theprint.in/defence/indian-navy-team-in-germany-to-inspect-aip-tech-for-new-submarines-spain-next/2027506/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250628150504/https://theprint.in/defence/indian-navy-team-in-germany-to-inspect-aip-tech-for-new-submarines-spain-next/2027506/ |archive-date=2025-06-28 |access-date=2026-01-10 |work=ThePrint |language=en-US}}</ref>

As of February 2025, development proposal for the [[Cabinet Committee on Security]] (CCS) approval would be ready by 2 months. The inter-ministerial consultation was underway. Post approval, two to three years would be required for design phase followed by five years for construction and induction. The submarines would be equipped with [[torpedo tube]]-launched [[Land-attack cruise missile|land-attack cruise missiles]] and displace 3,000 tonnes. The indigenous content is expected to be 90-95%. Imports will only include some chips, electronics, and tubes.<ref name=":12">{{Cite news |last=Peri |first=Dinakar |date=2025-02-22 |title=DRDO indigenous submarine proposal to go for CCS approval in couple of months; eight years for first sub |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/drdo-indigenous-submarine-proposal-to-go-for-ccs-approval-in-couple-of-months-eight-years-for-first-sub/article69251317.ece |access-date=2025-02-22 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref> The submarine will include indigenous [[Fire-control system|weapon control systems]] and [[lithium-ion batteries]]. The construction of the first submarine would begin in 2028.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-02-14 |title=Next Generation Submarine – Project 76 |url=https://www.spsnavalforces.com/experts-speak/?id=778&h=Next-Generation-Submarine-Project-76 |access-date=2026-01-10 |website=www.spsnavalforces.com}}</ref> This feature is unique to this design.<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 January 2023|title=Scorpene subs to be retro-fitted with the DRDO's air-independent propulsion (AIP), under Naval Group's oversight|url=https://www.ajaishukla.com/2023/01/scorpene-subs-to-be-retro-fitted-with.html|website=www.ajaishukla.com|quote=The AIP developed by the NMRL is called “fuel cell based AIP” and is unique in generating its requirement of hydrogen onboard.}}</ref><ref name=":14">{{Cite news |date=2021-03-09|title=Fuel Cell based Air Independent Propulsion (AIP) System Crosses Important Milestone of User Specific Tests|url=https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1703456&s=08|access-date=2024-12-30|work=[[Press Information Bureau]]|quote=While there are different types of AIP systems being pursued internationally, fuel cell-based AIP of NMRL is unique as the hydrogen is generated onboard.}}</ref>

The development is scheduled for completion by 2026–27 followed by construction of first submarine in 6–7 years and all six to be delivered within ten years. A 15-year roadmap, named Technology Perspective and Capability Roadmap 2025 (TPCR-25), unveiled development multiple key components for an Indigenous Conventional Submarine.<ref name=":10" /> Meanwhile, MDL and [[Larsen & Toubro]] have demonstrated ''[[Indian Navy Swimmer Delivery Vehicle#Mazagon Dockyard (MS-X02A)|Arowana]]'' and [[Indian Navy Swimmer Delivery Vehicle#Larsen & Toubro (SOV-400)|SOV-400]], respectively. MDL is also reportedly undertaken simultaneous design and development of full-scale indigenous conventional submarine by 2028.<ref name=":10" />
